_note: Regression ceilings, not targets: they exist to catch growth nobody decided on. Raised twice during the Castalia completion campaign, and the second time is worth being uncomfortable about — a ceiling raised whenever it is hit is not a ceiling. Both raises are recorded rather than quietly applied, and both were preceded by a real attempt to meet the existing number. First raise (2026-07-31): the pre-campaign numbers predated the refraction pass, the scene cue director, Attunement, the reading surfaces and the citations; drei deep imports were tried and returned 92 bytes, and code splitting does not help a metric that measures total JavaScript rather than the initial chunk. Second raise (2026-08-01): the conclusion is now performed by the scene rather than compiled and discarded, which cost about 2 kB gzip; the owning change first cut its own module by 25 percent minified and got 190 bytes of gzip back for it, so the remainder could not be found without deleting the feature. That note ended by saying that if a third raise were ever proposed, the right answer was probably to make the metric measure the initial chunk and let the conclusion load with the conclusion. THIS IS THAT CHANGE, AND IT IS NOT A THIRD RAISE (2026-08-03). The Schell design-review pass arrived with 1,459 bytes of gzip headroom against eight findings, so the prescription was taken instead of the ceiling: ConclusionScreen is behind a dynamic import — prefetched the moment the arena opens, so a player has twelve to eighteen minutes of warm-up and Suspense never actually suspends — Vite emits a manifest, and report-bundle.mjs walks the entry chunk's transitive STATIC imports to measure what a stranger downloads before the title appears. initialJavascriptGzipBytes is set to 524000, which is exactly what total JavaScript was allowed to reach before this change: 'the first load may not exceed what the whole bundle used to be allowed to be' is a line somebody can defend, and picking a fresh number that clears today's measurement by a comfortable margin is not. That turns 1,459 bytes of headroom into 9,013. WHAT IS GATED, AND WHY. initialJavascript* is the binding gate and the one to argue with, because it is what is paid before anything is seen. largestAssetRawBytes catches a texture or a font dropped in without looking. totalRawBytes and totalGzipBytes are raised once here, deliberately and generously, and their job has changed: they no longer block feature work, they only catch runaway growth in deferred code — a tight total is exactly what made deferring worthless and produced the two raises above. Total JavaScript is now reported under 'observed' and gated by nothing; note that it went UP by about 2 kB when the chunk was split, which is the plainest possible demonstration of why it was the wrong thing to fail a build on. If initialJavascriptGzipBytes is ever the thing standing between this project and a change worth making, the answer is another dynamic import, not another number.
